newsitem.title: HUNGARY: PHILIPS TO BUILD $30MLN PLANT IN HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS TO BUILD $30MLN PLANT IN HUNGARY.

text.p: Dutch-dased electronics group Philips announced on Thursday it is to invest $30 million over the next four years in a new plant in the western Hungarian city of Gyor.
The venture will initally employ 600, rising later to 1,000, Philips' Hungarian affiliate said in a statement.
The plant will initially produce car audio cassette decks, with production rising to five million units a year for delivery to countries throughout Europe.
"We hope that the presence of this factory will also attract a number of subcontractors...Some of these are already planning to open facilities on the same site," the statement said.

It cited the main reasons for building the factory in Gyor as the educated workforce, relatively low costs and good infrastructure. Gyor is situated near the Austrian border on the main Budapest-Vienna motoroway.
